title: Depthwise convolution
goal:
The convolution module of the Conformer block (Section 2.2) uses a single 1-D depthwise convolution. Each channel has its own filter, and the filter slides along time without mixing channels.

Write `depthwise_conv1d(x, w)`. `x` is a NumPy array of shape `(T, d)`: `T` frames and `d` channels. `w` has shape `(k, d)`: one length-`k` filter per channel. Return an array of shape `(T, d)` with

$$
y[t, c] = \sum_{i=0}^{k-1} w[i, c] \cdot x_{\text{pad}}[t + i, c]
$$

where `x_pad` is `x` padded with zeros along time: `(k - 1) // 2` frames at the start and `k - 1 - (k - 1) // 2` at the end. This keeps the length at `T` for odd and even `k`. The paper's kernel size is 32, which is even. The padding rule is this page's choice, because the paper doesn't state one. Do not flip the filter: this is cross-correlation, as in deep learning libraries.
hints: Pad with `np.pad(x, ((left, right), (0, 0)))`. Pad only along the time axis.
Start with a loop over the `k` filter taps. For tap `i`, the slice `xp[i:i + T]` holds the frames that line up with `w[i]`.
Multiply the slice by `w[i]` (shape `(d,)`, which broadcasts across time) and add it to the output. No tap ever combines two channels.
For an impulse at one frame, the output is the filter laid out around that frame. With `k = 3` and `w = [1, 2, 3]`, an impulse at frame 3 gives 3, 2, 1 at frames 2, 3, 4.
